label: Integrating along a path
subgoals: Write a line integral as a t-integral
Notice that direction changes the sign

visual.title: Direction changes the sign
visual.caption: The line integral walks around the loop and adds the component of the field along the step. Reversing the walk reverses every step, so the whole sum changes sign.

predict.question: Reversing the direction of a path changes a line integral how?
predict.explain: Every step dr changes sign, so ∫F·dr changes sign. On this loop the circulation is 2πr² and the reverse walk gives −2πr².
